record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Characterize the frontier of S-separable topological groups, where a topological group G is S-separable if, for every topological group H whose closed subgroups are all separable, every closed subgroup of G x H is separable. In particular: is every separable locally compact group S-separable; is the additive group of real numbers with its Euclidean topology S-separable; does there exist a separable metrizable group that is not S-separable; and is the free topological group on the closed unit interval [0,1] S-separable?

evidence.quote: Let us say that a topological group G is strongly separable (briefly, S-separable) if for any topological group H such that every closed subgroup of H is separable, the product G x H has each of its closed subgroups separable.
Find the frontiers of the class of S-separable topological groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a topological group $G$ S-separable if for every topological group $H$ in which every closed subgroup is separable, every closed subgroup of the product $G \times H$ is separable. 

Determine the frontiers of the class of S-separable topological groups. In particular, resolve the following:

1. Is every separable locally compact topological group S-separable?
2. Is the additive group $(\mathbb{R}, +)$ of real numbers with its usual Euclidean topology S-separable?
3. Does there exist a separable metrizable topological group that fails to be S-separable?
4. Is the free topological group $F([0,1])$ on the closed unit interval $[0,1]$ S-separable?

(Recall that a topological space is separable if it contains a countable dense subset, and that the free topological group $F(X)$ on a Tychonoff space $X$ is the unique topological group containing $X$ as a topological subspace, algebraically free on $X$, with the universal property that every continuous map from $X$ into a topological group extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism from $F(X)$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of S-separability and the request to characterize the frontiers of this class are posed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on separability of topological groups (Leiderman–Morris, Axioms 2019). No subsequent paper resolving the listed sub-questions (locally compact case, $\mathbb{R}$, separable metrizable counterexamples, free topological group on $[0,1]$) was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey presenting separability results in topological groups, with twenty open problems including those on S-separability.
status_evidence.claim: The S-separability frontier problem is posed as an open problem in this survey.
